setting: A fictional live support chat for a small software company that sells online booking tools.

presentation.situation: You support customers of a booking tool. {{name}} runs {{business}} and cannot {{problem}}. Your records show: {{record}}. Find out what is going on, explain it clearly without jargon, and agree what happens next.
presentation.opening: Hi, I run {{business}}, and I can't {{problem}}. Customers are asking me about it. Can you help?

brief.you_are: You are a customer support specialist for an online booking tool.
brief.situation: {{name}} runs {{business}} and cannot {{problem}}. Your records show: {{record}}. {{name}} is not technical.
brief.task: Ask about what is happening, explain the cause in plain words, and check that {{name}} understands the next step.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} understands the cause and what to do, in plain language, and you have checked that it makes sense.

participants.name: You
goals: Solve the problem in plain language

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: A small business owner using your booking tool

card.want: To get bookings working again before the next customers arrive.
card.hidden_need: Worries about looking unprofessional to regular customers.
card.attitude: Polite, stressed, and easily lost by technical words.
card.speech: Everyday English. Says plainly when something sounds too technical.
tactics: Ask 'what does that mean?' if you hear a technical word
Only describe what appears on your own screen when asked

pressure.challenging: Gets more anxious and asks how long this will take.

ledger.text: {{name}} runs {{business}} and uses the booking tool.
{{name}} did not change anything on purpose.

objectives.description: Find out what the customer is seeing
objectives.evidence: The learner asks a specific question about what happens or what appears, before explaining.
alternatives: What do you see on your screen when you try?

objectives.description: Explain the cause and fix in plain language
objectives.evidence: The learner explains what happened and what to do without unexplained technical terms.
alternatives: Your calendar got disconnected, so let's link it again

objectives.description: Check understanding and agree the next step
objectives.evidence: The learner checks that it makes sense or worked, and agrees what happens next.
alternatives: Does that make sense? Try it now and tell me what you see

examples: What do you see on your screen?
In simple terms, what happened is ...
Does that make sense? Could you try it now?
prerequisites: Read the support record in the briefing.

beats.goal: The customer needs to be asked what they actually see.
signals: \b(?:what do you see|what happens|on your screen|what (?:does|did) it say|when did|error|can you tell me|what message)\b
opportunity: I don't know what else to tell you. Do you need to know what's on my screen?
My customers are waiting. What do you need from me?
beats.orient: You're supporting me with the booking tool. First, ask me what I can see on my screen.
fallback: What do you need to know from me?
Do you want me to tell you what's on my screen?

beats.goal: The customer needs the cause and the fix without jargon.
signals: \b(?:happened|because|what you need to|in simple|the reason|you can fix|click|open|go to|link|turn on|turn off)\b
opportunity: Sorry, what does that mean in normal words?
beats.orient: Look at the record in your brief and tell me what went wrong and what I should do. Please use simple words.
fallback: So what's wrong, in normal words?

beats.goal: Make sure the customer can do it, and knows what happens next.
signals: \b(?:does that make sense|is that clear|try (?:it|that)|let me know|are you able|did that work|any questions|what do you see now)\b
opportunity: I think I follow. What happens if it doesn't work?
So is that everything I need to do?
beats.orient: Nearly done. Check that I understood you, and tell me what happens next if it doesn't work.
fallback: Is that everything I need to do?

closing_line: That's a relief. Thank you, that was easy to follow.

o1.good: Asking what the customer sees before giving an answer, so you solve the real problem.
common_mistakes: Asking for technical details they can't know
o1.micro_lesson: Ask what they see. Customers can describe a screen, even when they can't name the problem.
o1.model: What do you see on your screen when you try to take a booking?
o1.smaller_step: Ask the customer one question about their screen.

o2.good: Saying what happened in everyday words, then one clear action.
common_mistakes: Explaining everything instead of the next step
o2.micro_lesson: Replace technical words with what the person will see or do.
o2.model: Your calendar got disconnected, so bookings stopped. Let's link it again together.
o2.smaller_step: Say the one thing they should do first.

o3.good: Checking it worked, and saying what happens next if it didn't.
o3.micro_lesson: Finish by checking. Ask them to try it, and say what you'll do if it fails.
o3.model: Could you try it now? If it still doesn't work, I'll call you back within the hour.

variants.name: Bilal
variants.screen: a message saying the calendar is not connected
variants.record: the calendar link expired last night
variants.fix: open Settings and connect the calendar again

variants.name: Rosa
variants.problem: see this week's classes on my booking page
variants.screen: an empty booking page with a note saying no classes are published
variants.record: this week's classes were saved as drafts
variants.fix: open the class list and press Publish

variants.name: Kamran
variants.problem: get paid through my booking page
variants.screen: a warning that card payments are switched off
variants.record: the payment account needs its details confirmed
variants.fix: open Payments and confirm the account details
